voyage.name: Schloss Hellbrunn
voyage.price: Adults €13.50, students (19-26 years old) €8.50, children (4-18 years) €6.00, family ticket (2 adults, 1 child) €29.50
voyage.hours: Apr Oct: 09:00-16:30; May Jun Sep: 09:00-17:30; Jul Aug: 09:00-21:00 (only trick fountains from 18:00)
voyage.content: Once the summer palace of the Archbishops of Salzburg it has lots of clever fountains and pretty gardens. When you take the tour stand next to the guide otherwise you will get wet. Hellbrunn is surrounded by vast gardens, including a good children's playground with swings and flying fox (zip wire), and a cold wading pool, and is a perfect place for a picnic or a long walk through the green. In the Steintheater (Stone

voyage.name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
voyage.content: On top of a mountain, the Festung offers breathtaking views of Salzburg and the Alps. One area of the fortress offers visitors the chance to look down on a field below to find only one house, the executioner's residence. It was believed to live anywhere near the executioner was bad luck. Inside the fortress is a museum of medieval weapons, life on the fortress, and torture instruments. Public concerts are often held

voyage.name: Alter Markt Square
voyage.content: Various shops in this area are quite old and impressive. For instance have a look at the interior of the pharmacy called Fürsterzbischöfliche Apotheke. No pictures though, this is a pharmacy not a tourist attraction.

voyage.name: Schloss Mirabell
voyage.content: Next to the Salzach river and the Mozarteum University of Music and Arts lies a beautiful castle with gardens, built by an archbishop for his beloved courtesan. Watch out for the "Garden of Dwarfs" and the Garden of Roses. Inside, you find the marble stairs of Raffael Donner, and the world's most beautiful wedding hall, the Marble Hall. If you plan to marry there, reservations should be made at least a year in advanc

voyage.name: Salzburg Cathedral
voyage.price: 5 EUR + 3 EUR for the audio guide
voyage.content: In Cathedral Excavations Museum you can see objects excavated from a Roman villa and foundations of the west towers of the Romanesque cathedral both of which stood in the area of today's cathedral.

voyage.name: Getreidegasse
voyage.content: A long yet narrow street running parallel to the river in the centre of town, with lots of shops, famous for the old (or old-style) signs of profession outside each store.

voyage.name: St. Sebastian Cemetery
voyage.content: Holds the graves of Mozart's wife Constanze Weber-Nissen, and the must-see Mausoleum of Archbishop Wolfdietrich.

voyage.name: St Peter's Church, Cemetery, and Catacombs
voyage.hours: Catacombs: May-Sep: daily 10:00-12:30 13:00-18:00, Oct-Apr: 10:00-12:30 13:00-17:00; cemetery: Apr-Sep: daily 06:30-20:00, Oct-Mar: daily 06:30-18:00; church: daily 08:00-20:00
voyage.content: Perhaps most remarkable are the small catacombs (€2 adults, €1.50 children) carved into the nearby cliff side. Climb up for a couple of small chapels and a nice overlook.

voyage.name: Hellbrunn Trick Fountains
voyage.content: Park with trick fountains.

voyage.name: Nonnberg Abbey
voyage.content: Founded around 711/712 by Saint Rupert, the Nonnberg Abbey is the world's oldest continuously operating Christian convent. Situated on a terrace of Salzburg's Festungsberg, it has been a significant religious site for centuries. The abbey church, dedicated to the Assumption of Mary, showcases architectural elements from the Romanesque and Gothic periods, with notable frescoes and a prominent tower. Explore the church

voyage.name: Mozarts Geburtshaus
voyage.price: Adults €10, youths and school groups 15-18 €4, children and school groups 6-14 €3.50, family tickets (2 adults with children) €21
voyage.content: From 1747 to 1773 the Mozart family lived in this house in the heart of Salzburg, where W.A. Mozart was born on 27 January 1756. The house is now a popular museum devoted to Mozart and his family, with interesting memorabilia and letters. Well worth a quick visit.

voyage.name: Mozarts Wohnhaus
voyage.price: Adults €10 (with birth house €17), youths and school groups 15-18 €4, children 6-14 €3.50, family €21
voyage.content: Mozart’s Residence was reconstructed after being destroyed during World War II and was opened to the public in 1996.

voyage.name: Salzburg Museum
voyage.price: Adults €8.50, 16-26 years €4, 6-15 years €3, families (2 adults and children) €17, seniors €7, people with impairment (ID) or Salzburg Card free. Combi Ticket with the Panorama Museum: adults €10, 16-26 €4.50, 6-15 €3.50, families €20, seniors €8.50, people with impairment (ID) or Salzburg Card free
voyage.content: Trying really hard to tell you about Salzburg's history. Blind and partner dogs may be taken to the museum. There are regular guided tours for blind/visually impaired and deaf/hearing impaired people. Call for an appointment. All rooms of the Salzburg Museum in the Neue Residenz are wheelchair accessible. A passenger lift with sufficient door width leads to all floors. In the New Residence there is an induction loop

voyage.name: Toy Museum
voyage.content: Founded in 1978, the Toy Museum has the largest collection in Austria of European toys. The "Kasperltheater" puppet show has been held every Tuesday and Wednesday at 15:00 for the since the early 1990s.

voyage.name: Museum of Natural History
voyage.price: Adults €8.50, seniors (60+) or with a pass €8, students (under 27) and children (4+) €6 (2019)
voyage.content: Science museum in the heart of the city. It offers interactive exhibits covering a wide range of topics, from natural history and geology to physics and astronomy. Highlights include a large collection of local and exotic wildlife, a fascinating look at the universe through the museum's planetarium, and an extensive exhibition on the history of the Earth.

voyage.name: Salzburg Museum of Modern Art
voyage.content: Two locations: Wiener Philharmonikergasse 9, and Mönchsberg 32. The Salzburg Museum of Modern Art is on the cliff overlooking the old town. It houses contemporary art works from the 20th and 21st centuries, along with rotating international art displays.

voyage.name: Residenzgalerie
voyage.content: Art gallery showcasing European paintings from the 16th to 19th centuries. Established in 1923 to revive Salzburg's artistic heritage, the gallery's notable collections include the Czernin Collection, featuring 17th-century Dutch, Italian, Spanish, and French masterpieces, and works from the Schönborn-Buchheim Collection, highlighting Dutch and Italian artists of the same era. Some of the more famous painters include

voyage.name: Hangar 7
voyage.content: Transportation museum housing the historical Flying Bulls fleet and several historic race cars. The collection itself will not be too spectacular unless you're a race fanatic, but the building itself with its glass domed roof is worth a visit.

voyage.name: Hallein Salt Mine
voyage.content: An ancient underground salt mine on the Dürrnberg plateau near Hallein. With a history spanning over 2,600 years, it was instrumental in establishing Salzburg as a significant trading hub. Today, the mine operates as a museum, offering guided tours that include a 400-metre electric train ride into the mountain, wooden slides between levels, and a boat trip across an underground salt lake. Visitors don protective cove

voyage.name: Stiegl Brauwelt
voyage.content: Brewery museum offering an immersive experience into the world of beer. You can explore interactive exhibits detailing the brewing process, enjoy freshly tapped Stiegl beer in one of the on-site restaurants, and purchase souvenirs from the brewery shop. Guided tours available at 15:00.

voyage.name: Salzburg open-air museum
voyage.content: The 50-hectare Salzburg Open-Air Museum is located southwest of the city on the Untersberg. The Salzburg Open-Air Museum consists of around 100 original buildings spanning 6 centuries. There are old farms, a brewery, village school, blacksmith shop, power station, old tractors, steam engines and work tools, as well as a historic inn with a cozy garden. Especially on Sundays and public holidays, artisans demonstrate t

voyage.name: Kapuzinerberg
voyage.content: This steep hill can be accessed through Linzergasse in the old part of town. Once you're in you're in deep forest. There are several paths that bring you to the top (where the Franziskischlössl fortification stands - today it's a restaurant) via either a paved road -no traffic, though- or a forest track with steps. There are several viewpoints along the way. The views of the city, and the Alps, are spectacular, the a

voyage.name: Untersberg
voyage.content: The Untersberg is a striking mountain on the Austria-Germany border, easily accessible from Salzburg. Take the Untersbergbahn cable car to Geiereck peak (1,776 m) for stunning Alpine views. The area offers hiking, climbing, and winter sports, with trails suitable for all levels. Bus 25 connects Salzburg to the cable car station, making it a convenient day trip.

voyage.name: Lammer Gorge
voyage.price: Adults: €10 (with Tennengau Plus Card €9, with the Salzburg Family Pass €8); groups (adults, 15 or more people): €9; children (ages 6 to 15): €7 (with Family Pass: €6); with the Salzburger Land Card admission is free
voyage.content: A natural canyon carved by the Lammer River near Scheffau am Tennengebirge. This 1 km long gorge features dramatic limestone formations and narrow passages, with a height difference of 43 m. Explore the trail that winds through the gorge, offering stunning views of the rushing river and surrounding cliffs. The trail is accessible for a fee and has been in place since 1884. At both the upper and lower entrances of the

voyage.name: Casino Salzburg
voyage.hours: Open daily except for December 24. Slot machines: 12:00-03:00, Live games: 15:00-03:00

voyage.name: Salzburg Zoo
voyage.content: The zoo is in south Salzburg and is open 365 days a year. It also has a petting zoo for children. There is a restaurant on site serving traditional Austrian dishes.

voyage.name: Untersberg
voyage.content: The mountain is perennially popular with tourists due to its proximity to the city of Salzburg, less than 16 km to the north of the mountain and within easy reach by bus. A variety of paths lead to the top, but most people use the cable car that lifts passengers over 1300m to the Geiereck peak. The cable car runs from the station in the town of Gartenau to the station at the Geiereck peak. Can be reached from Salzbur

voyage.name: Europark
voyage.content: Indoor shopping mall. Nothing out of the ordinary, but a good place to take refuge if the weather is poor.

voyage.name: Salzburger Würstelkönigin
voyage.content: Gorgeous hotdogs and great spot to chill by the Salzburg river. The grilled meat sandwich with the Century Sauce (Jahrhundertsoße) is amazing. You can meet the whole world here.

voyage.name: Heisse Kiste
voyage.content: An institution. Recommended are the Leberkäs and the Käsekrainer. Real sausage culture - very tasty. One of the most popular addresses among the people enjoying Salzburg's nightlife to grab a sausage with bread for a midnight snack.

voyage.name: Lechners Würstelstand!
voyage.content: If you want to try Austria's original street food in Salzburg, this is the place to go. Very traditional, very tasty. Service is fast. Everything is delicious.

voyage.name: Würstelstand Alter Markt
voyage.content: The Käsekrainer and the warm sauerkraut are delicious. Tasty fries, Bosna and whatever the sausage heart desires. There might be a queue and then it takes some time...

voyage.name: Maroni-Salzburg
voyage.content: Have roasted chestnuts and a glass of glühwein in the winter season right before you start off to the Christmas Market. Maronibraterei Salzburg

voyage.name: Wilder Mann
voyage.content: Wilder Mann offers traditional Austrian cuisine. The restaurant provides large portions and friendly-service. Smoking is allowed in the restaurant.

voyage.name: Schmankerl
voyage.content: Affordable meals and you support a social project of the town of Salzburg. Very friendly staff, well attended. The meals are good.

voyage.name: Paninoteca Piccolo Mondo
voyage.content: A lovely selection of paninis that look really lovely and taste just like Italy. Quality wines and tasty pasta. Recommendation for the antipasti platter.

voyage.name: Burrito Factory
voyage.content: You feel like you are in a host family who has invited you to dinner in Mexico. You should reserve a table at lunchtime because the restaurant is quite small, which is exactly what makes it so charming. Very friendly service.

voyage.name: Pommes Boutique
voyage.content: A wonderful stop for those who love burgers and fries. Vegetarian options available. Outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Uncle Van
voyage.content: A lovely little place completely unexpected in an otherwise unremarkable street. Great concept to select the ingredients for your wok. Very tasty. Also everyone who wants to eat vegetarian is at the right place here.

voyage.name: Reyna Kebap
voyage.content: Great kebab and very good pizza until late at night. Super Bosna. Very nice staff.

voyage.name: Bärenwirt
voyage.content: Traditional food, traditionally furnished restaurant, rather cheap, fabulous beer from the close by Augustiner Bräu.

voyage.name: Gabler Bräu
voyage.content: Traditional food of high quality, a big selection of salads from the self-service-menu.

voyage.name: Gasthof Goldgasse
voyage.content: Seasonal, regional, and of the highest quality.

voyage.name: Goldener Stern
voyage.content: A good choice to enjoy "Salzburger Nockerln" as well as "Topfenstrudel". In the middle of its garden full of trees and flowers there´s an old Austrian stagecoach where children can play.

voyage.name: Raschhofer's Rossbräu
voyage.content: Traditional, yet somewhat updated, Austrian fare. They serve excellent "Kaiserschmnarrn" a "breakfast" (yet really a dessert).

voyage.name: Sternbräu
voyage.content: Charming venue featuring wood-paneled restaurants serving regional fare, plus pubs and beer gardens, complete with outdoor seating, a fireplace, and private dining rooms.

voyage.name: Zirkel Wirt
voyage.content: Delicious traditional and some not-so-traditional food, vegetarian-friendly, great beer, good atmosphere.

voyage.name: Hangar 7 / Ikarus
voyage.content: If you seek a special environment for your dinner this is the place, a top-cuisine restaurant and a great bar close to the airport.

voyage.name: KOLLER+KOLLER am Waagplatz - Restaurant & Tagesbar
voyage.content: Excellent Austrian fare in a romantic intimate setting. Just steps away from the Salzburg Cathedral on Mozart Plaza. A 3-course meal for two people with a bottle of wine was about €90.

voyage.name: Stiftskeller St. Peter
voyage.content: Claims to have been opened in 803, and as such the oldest restaurant in the world. Austrian cuisine with some Mediterranean influences in a quite grandiose environment.

voyage.name: Restaurant Blaue Gans
voyage.content: Traditional and noble. Great 'Schnitzel'.

voyage.name: Café Sacher Salzburg
voyage.content: Trying the original Sacher-Torte is a must for all chocolate lovers out there. But there's more to Café Sacher than just cake. They also serve delicious hot food at prices cheaper than other touristy places listed here - plus you enjoy the service and ambiance of the Sacher Hotel.

voyage.name: Augustiner Bräustübl
voyage.content: Augustine monks have been brewing here since 1621. Today it's Austria's largest beer hall, with a lovely garden outside when the weather is nice and enormous inside halls when it isn't. Grab a table, a few ceramic steins of Märzenbier beer straight from the barrel, and pick your favorite Austrian dishes from the market-style shops. Or you can bring your own food (not drinks!) if you want.

voyage.name: The Shamrock
voyage.content: Guinness, cider, German and Austrian beer as well, occasional live music, and a nice atmosphere. Popular with local university students. Expect the place to be packed on a weekend night.

voyage.name: Stiegl Brauwelt
voyage.content: Bus stop Bräuhausstrasse on line 1. Tour the brewery and museum and have a Stiegl in the brewery's own pub and beer garden. The tour costs €9 and it includes three 20cl drinks and a gift.

voyage.name: Stieglkeller
voyage.content: The Stieglkeller is open from May to September. It offers a small choice of traditional dishes, Stiegl beers, Radler and other drinks. It is most recommendable for its fantastic panoramic view over the city. The lower terrace is with service, though you are expected to consume food there. The upper two terraces are self-service areas.

voyage.name: O'Malley's
voyage.content: Everyone goes here. Great bartenders. Open late for real drinkers.

voyage.name: Die Weisse
voyage.content: Located in one of Salzburg's most historic breweries, this is where all the locals hang out. It's best to make reservations Wednesday through Saturday as it can get crowded. They also serve treats from Bavaria and Salzburg!

voyage.name: Tomaselli
voyage.content: Alter Markt 9. A traditional Viennese coffee house, the oldest in Salzburg. Try the Einspänner and Sacher cake!

voyage.name: Café Bazar
voyage.content: Legendary Viennese coffee house with terrace overlooking the river Salzach and the city, where artists and businessmen alike (and yes, tourists as well) sip a "Kleiner Brauner" and discuss last evening's Festival-performance.

voyage.name: Fürst
voyage.content: Exquisite pastries, and the place to buy the original Mozartkugel, invented by confectioner Paul Fürst in 1884.

voyage.name: Republic
voyage.content: A modern café with good breakfast, and a variety of cultural events (Jazz Brunch, Clubbing, special theme parties at night). Turns into one of the most popular places to be during night.

voyage.name: Shakespeare
voyage.content: Art café with good Chinese cuisine, cheap lunch menu during the week.

voyage.name: Anifer Mühlenbrot
voyage.content: A tiny bakery with a tasty selection of sweets and snacks, and serves cheap breakfast, even though there is only one table. Try the Berger chocolates.

voyage.name: Afro Café
voyage.content: A funky, modern café with decoration inspired by urban African style. Offers a variety of unconventional and great food and drinks.

voyage.name: Café Sacher Salzburg
voyage.content: Excellent coffee (try the Wiener Melange if you like your cappuccinos) and great cakes and desserts. The Sacher-Torte hardly requires an introduction. But there are more cakes and tortes. The Strudel is great, and if you have a big appetite the Kaiserschmarrn (huge pancake-like dessert with plum confit and lots of sugar!) will not disappoint you. And it's not as expensive as you might imagine given this is a 5-star h

voyage.name: Nord-Sam
voyage.content: Decent sized site with a pool, shop, washing facilities, and on a bus route. By car via A1 Salzburg-Wien (Vienna), exit Salzburg-Nord. Follow signs to Nord-Sam after the traffic lights. Takes about 20 minutes to get into the city and is in a peaceful residential area with a supermarket (Spar) a short walk away.

voyage.name: Hotel Lasserhof Salzburg
voyage.content: This family-run hotel is located within walking distance of the Mirabell Castle and Gardens. Breakfast is included, and is served 07:00-12:00. There is also free Internet access.

voyage.name: Youth and Family Guesthouse Salzburg - Hostelling International
voyage.content: Renovated hostel. Breakfast and linens included. Amenities included: internet, café/bar, and a common room. The Sound of Music is shown nightly at 20:00 in the common room.

voyage.name: YoHo (International Youth Hotel Salzburg)
voyage.content: The Youth Hotel offers guests clean rooms at reasonable prices. They also show The Sound of Music every morning at 10:30.

voyage.name: Landesberufsschülerheim Aigen - Hosteling International
voyage.content: This hostel has 156 beds and a fitness room.

voyage.name: Landesberufsschülerheim Haunspergstraße - Hosteling International
voyage.content: 24 rooms all with an attached washroom and Internet access.

voyage.name: Eduard Heinrich Haus - Hosteling International
voyage.content: The hostel is open 365 days a year, and offers its guests Internet and a TV room. Most of the rooms have an attached washroom. Prices start from €16.

voyage.name: Muffin Hostel Salzburg
voyage.content: The hostel is opened from 13 July till 6 September and offers wide range of facilities, great location and superb prices starting from €21.

voyage.name: A&O Hostel Salzburg Hauptbahnhof
voyage.content: Rooms for couples, groups and families for very cheap rates. Close to the main train station.

voyage.name: Gasthaus Hinterbrühl
voyage.content: Edge of old town in a building constructed in 1380, the plumbing is slightly more modern.

voyage.name: AllYouNeed Hotel Salzburg
voyage.content: The hotel is open from 1 July to 30 September and has 69 non-smoking rooms en-suite with hairdryer, flat-TV with cable access, telephone and free internet, 1 handicapped accessible room, breakfast buffet and breakfast room with a panorama terrace overlooking the rooftops of Salzburg, lift, lobby with seating, parking (extra charge), luggage storage, concierge service.

voyage.name: Amade Hotel Schaffenrath
voyage.content: Located in the southern section of Salzburg, this hotel has 48 rooms and 28 apartments. Rooms start from €75 and include breakfast.

voyage.name: City Hotel Wolf-Dietrich
voyage.content: The hotel has rooms decorated in a classic style. Each room has a private bathroom and minibar. The hotel also offers its guests an organic breakfast buffet. Rooms start from €75 and vary according to season.

voyage.name: Hotel Haus Arenberg
voyage.content: Quietly located on a slope of the Kapuzinerberg this Hotel Garni "House Arenberg" offers a special kind of stay. The view of the City with its breathtaking mountain panorama as well as the sophisticated atmosphere of the Salzburgian lifestyle give the feeling of country-live in the midst of the city.

voyage.name: Hotel-Pension Adlerhof
voyage.content: A small family-run bed & breakfast, very close to the train station. The hotel offers free wireless internet and bike rentals. 24-hour reception.

voyage.name: Hotel Auersperg
voyage.content: Part of the Golden Tulip chain but with an independent feel, this hotel is just off the Linzergasse, close to all old town sights and a pleasant 5-10 min walk into the city centre. Free mulled wine, a fantastic rooftop sauna/spa/winter garden complex (also free) and free wi-fi internet access all over the hotel. Breakfast buffet included and served until 11:00.

voyage.name: Hotel Trumer Stube
voyage.content: Family-run three-star hotel just off the Linzergasse, close to all old town sights. Hosts are exceptionally friendly and knowledgeable. Breakfast buffet included.

voyage.name: Ambiente-Hotel Struber
voyage.content: Family-run hotel, set in a central location, with spacious rooms, near the old town, yet surrounded by meadows. Rooms reflecting Salzburg tradition, feature shower (or bath tub), toilet, phone, satellite TV and radio. Some rooms have balcony with view of Salzburg Castle.Car park right in front of the hotel.

voyage.name: NH Salzburg City
voyage.content: This 4-star hotel offers comfortable rooms and is located in the heart of the city. The hotel itself is very modern and offers many amenities to make the stay very comfortable.

voyage.name: Hotel Weisse Taube
voyage.content: Situated in the center of the old town, Hotel Weisse Taube has been owned by the same family for over a hundred years. Now a four star hotel and fully renovated, it has retained the spirit of the 700 year old citizen house.

voyage.name: Hotel Goldgasse (ehem. Zur Goldenen Ente)
voyage.content: Very nice hotel set in a central location.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn
voyage.content: Well furnished rooms. Reasonable breakfast, good service. A little way out of the centre of town. Has parking, some free, mostly paid.

voyage.name: Hotel Goldener Hirsch
voyage.content: This 65-room hotel is across from the Festival Hall and down the street from Mozart's house. The friendly staff is happy to help with all one's business needs. The hotel also has a 24-hour in-room dining and nightly turndown services.

voyage.name: Hotel Schloss Mönchstein
voyage.content: This hotel is comprised of 24 rooms, each equipped with a minibar and a wireless internet power point. There is also a restaurant on site; reservations are recommended. Prices vary according to the season.

voyage.name: Best Western Hotel Elefant
voyage.content: One of Salzburg's most ancient buildings, over 700 years old. The hotel is in a quiet alley off the world-famous Getreidegasse. Over the hotel's 400-year history, its purpose was, and still is, to serve its guests according to the best in Austrian tradition.

voyage.name: Schwärzler Hotel Neutor
voyage.content: Schwärzler Hotel Neutor, known as the artists' meeting place, is located close to the city center. Breakfast is served until 13:00 in your room or until 15:00 in the hotel's 'Artist Cafe.'.

voyage.name: Hotel Hölle
voyage.content: Hotel Hölle is comprised of 15 rooms, and is on the edge of the city center. The hotel has various sized rooms to suite your level of comfort. The on site restaurant, À la Carte, serves the best of Austrian cuisine, and is open daily from 08:00-12:00.

voyage.name: Romantik & Spa Hotel Gmachl
voyage.content: - On the green outskirts of the city, just about an 8 km drive from Salzburg’s historic heart, you will find the Romantik Hotel Gmachl, the oldest family-run establishment in all of Austria (established in 1334). The hotel offers 35 luxurious rooms, an accredited restaurant and an exclusive Spa & Beauty area, boasting a bio-sauna, infrared cabin, aroma steam bath, fitness room, mist grotto, tanning studio and an outd

voyage.name: Hotel Bergrose
voyage.content: Hotel Bergrose is a very romantic hotel at the legendary Wolfgangsee close to Salzburg.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Altstadt Hotel Salzburg
voyage.content: 5 Stars. Very comfortable, in a traditional building of Salzburg's old town. Breakfast is also really good.

en.title: Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg
